Q1: Manganese dichloride presents a hazard profile primarily marked by known significant concerns (Tier 1) for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive hazards (CMR), environmental hazards (ENV), oral hazards (ORL), dermal and eye hazards (SKN), and organ/systemic hazards (OGN). Additionally, it shows evidence of potential endocrine disruption from an expanded data perspective (Tier 2 EDC). Its inhalation hazards (IHL) are considered low to moderate, supported by direct studies (Tier 3).
Q2: Manganese dichloride is identified on the TEDX list (The Endocrine Disruption Exchange), which designates it as a potential endocrine disruptor based on available scientific research. This classification aligns with its Tier 2 hazard rating for endocrine disruption.
Q3: Manganese dichloride is very well characterized, supported by an extensive body of scientific literature with 36,000 references, significantly exceeding the median for chemicals. Its molecular formula (Cl2Mn) is precisely defined, it is categorized as a 'Small Molecule,' and it is not an incompletely defined UVCB substance. The absence of any Tier 4 (data deficient) classifications across its hazard profile further indicates a comprehensive understanding of its risks.
